correctness.rationale: For p>=11, logarithmic weights -log(1-p^-3) form a complete finite-subsum interval because p-weight <= sum of higher-prime weights: six small-prime rational inequalities and Nagura q<6p/5 yield the full tail product [C,1]. The small primes 2,3,5,7 split into 4*2^3=32 exponent classes; C*U<L makes all [C*h,h] within each class mutually intersect, so the whole class is [C*L,U]. The actual verify.py is an exact rational certificate for zeta bounds, six prime-tail comparisons and 31 gap/overlap checks. A separate Python rational head enumeration plus 80-digit evaluation of C reproduced all 19 displayed ordered endpoints exactly: 13 overlaps and 18 strict gaps; this numerical calculation corroborates but does not substitute for the rigorous floor-sum rational comparison. All components nondegenerate; no bounded-n sampling is used for the infinite claim.
residual_risks: The infinite-prime step invokes Nagura’s established prime interval theorem, not a finite prime sample.
The independent high-precision C check is not itself a proof of strict inequalities; the source rational enclosure is the proof certificate.
